pr_title: Add ARRAY to test_all_types + IO and some clients
pr_body:
This PR adds:
- A bunch of different array types `test_all_types()`
- Support for array types/vectors in the C-API
- Support for array import and export in the JSON extension.
- Support for array import and export in the Parquet extension.
- Support for arrays in the Python client, both as python objects and as arrow fixed-size-lists.

This PR does __not__ add
- Support for array types in the Java client
- Support for array types in the Julia client

The tests in these clients based on `test_all_types` have been modified to exclude the new array entries. Im planning to add support for Java in a future PR.

In theory we could also support nested numpy arrays better now now that we have a proper fixed size array type, but this PR makes no changes to how that is handled, nested numpy arrays still become multiple columns.

Since Parquet doesn't have a fixed-size list type, you can't really roundtrip a written array back into DuckDB as you will just get a list type back instead. In the future we may want to annotate array columns with duckdb specific metadata to recognize this during import and perform the conversion (or insert a cast) automagically.

Also fixes some misc array bugs related to flattening.


Closes https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/10785
Closes https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/10667
Closes https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/10663

issue_context.title: Python connection does not support Array type
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

When I execute a query with `con = duckdb.connect(...); con.execute(query)` that uses the Array type it fails with:

_duckdb.duckdb.NotImplementedException: Not implemented Error: Unsupported type: "FLOAT[3]"_

note: no relevant extension was found related to the Array type and no extension was loaded into the connection.

### To Reproduce

* run the minimal python script below
* see that the NotImplementedException is raised

Minimal python script that reproduces the error:

```
import duckdb


with duckdb.connect() as con:

    con.execute("CREATE TABLE embeddings (id INTEGER, embedding FLOAT[3]);")
    con.execute("INSERT INTO embeddings VALUES (1, [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]);")

    result = con.execute("SELECT id, embedding FROM embeddings;")
    print(result.fetchall())

```


### OS:

Ubuntu 22.04

### DuckDB Version:

0.10.0

### DuckDB Client:

Python

### Full Name:

Luuk van der Velden

### Affiliation:

Codebeez

### Have you tried this on the latest [nightly build](https://duckdb.org/docs/installation/?version=main)?

I have tested with a nightly build

### Have you tried the steps to reproduce? Do they include all relevant data and configuration? Does the issue you report still appear there?

- [X] Yes, I have
comments: Where this breaks is in result collection, that's why `.sql(...)` didn't result in the error yet, when you use `.fetchall` it'll run into the same issue
Im working on adding support for this! You can cast the result to a list to work around this for now.
thank you @Maxxen ! Looking forward to your updates.

review_comments: This is rather complex code and it looks like it's mostly a copy-paste from the `ListColumnWriter::Prepare` - could we perhaps unify the code (or just cast arrays to lists for parquet writing? we have a `CastColumnReader` for reading, we could similarly consider creating a `CastColumnWriter` for writing)

The issue with unifying with the list is that we 1. don't have a list_entry_t child vector and 2. need to write validity differently. I think casting would be a good idea but I wasn't sure where to perform the cast. Ill have a look at the `CastColumnReader` and see if I can do something similar for the write-side.
We can't template virtual functions so we'd have to template the whole class
How about I just subclass the ListColumnWriter and override just Analyze, Prepare, Write?

The way you can test this is by using `duckdb.execute("query with prepared parameters", {"param_name": param})`

The `target_type` is tested by creating `duckdb.Value(obj, <type object>)`
When scanning the `duckdb.Value` object we unwrap it and pass the enclosed type object as `target_type`
Ive added a small test for this for just the array and list type ambiguity.
